items.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Lew Soloff? [INTERVIEWEE] I think that was before Lew.

ctx.x: on the jazz scene going way back: Howard Johnson, Johnny Coles, Jimmy Knepper I think was in the band at that point. I don’t remember whether Dave Sanborn was playing — no that came a little bit later. Lenny White was the drummer at that point and Herb Bushler was playing bass.

I think that was before Lew. It’s really close. Joe Beck played guitar with them somewhere in that period on and off. Joe was having a lot of trouble with his eyes so sometimes he just didn’t want to make club dates. But Billy Harper, Trevor Kohler, it goes on. But there were a lot of really strong soloists. And guys would stand up and take twenty choruses and it would be worth it. It was great. So I’m sitting there as a horn player and this went on for a while. And we’d play a head and then there would be twenty…
